narrative.summary: Samoa has no AI law or AI strategy. Its only AI-steering document is the National ICT Policy 2025/26-2030/31, launched in April 2026, which commits to responsible use of AI in digital government and to a future AI regulatory framework with the Office of the Regulator, alongside a planned data privacy framework.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT)
narrative.review_notes: This review was updated on 18 October 2026. The Office of the Regulator, the Ministry of Education and Culture, Parliament and the communications ministry were checked again and no new AI document was found. Not yet verified from the official text: AI provisions across consolidated law on the official legislation portal and the Attorney General's website; this remains pending.

instruments.official_title: National Communications & Information Technology Policy Samoa 2025/26 - 2030/31
instruments.english_title: National Information and Communications Technology Policy 2025/26-2030/31
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, Government of Samoa
instruments.current_status: Launched by the Deputy Prime Minister on 17 April 2026 at the close of Samoa Digital Week 2026, together with the National Cybersecurity Strategy 2025/26-2030/31; the published PDF leaves the Cabinet endorsement reference, effective date and approval date blank, so no effective date is recorded. It succeeds the National ICT Policy 2012-2017; Samoa has no standalone AI strategy or AI law.
instruments.summary: Samoa's national ICT policy for 2025/26-2030/31, organised in five pillars (connectivity and infrastructure, digital government, digital economy, leadership/coordination/governance, digital skills) with cybersecurity as a cross-cutting requirement. On AI it commits government to use AI responsibly in digital public services (priority 2.3), to establish and periodically update regulatory frameworks for emerging technologies including AI with the Office of the Regulator to manage risks while enabling innovation (priority 4.4, status 'not started'), and to build data and AI skills in the public service and among businesses (priorities 3.2, 5.3, 5.4). It also commits to enacting a data privacy framework (priority 3.1).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only national policy document that sets government expectations for AI: responsible AI use in digital government and a planned regulatory framework for AI; there is no dedicated AI pillar.

ICT Policy kept: explicit AI commitments (priority 2.3 responsible AI in digital government; 4.4 AI regulatory framework, 'Not started'); dated 2026-04-17 from MCIT launch notice (PDF approval fields blank). National Cybersecurity Strategy 2025/26-2030/31 mentions AI once (lead). Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: Parliament of Samoa (palemene.ws) bills/acts page and site search: no AI bill or act, no data protection bill, no deepfake offence found (list runs to 2023 bills). samoalaws.gov.ws could not be reached (proxy 502 / DNS failure via curl and WebFetch).
